title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Reissuing the Basic Standards for Judges' Professional Ethics of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Re-issuing the Basic Code of Ethics for Judges of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [2010] No. 53

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The revised Basic Code of Ethics for Judges of the People's Republic of China is hereby re-issued. Please earnestly implement and enforce it.

December 6, 2010

Basic Code of Ethics for Judges of the People's Republic of China

(Issued by the Supreme People's Court on October 18, 2001; revised and re-issued on December 6, 2010)

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 This Code is formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant provisions, for the purpose of strengthening the professional ethics of judges and ensuring that judges correctly perform the duties conferred upon them by law.

Article 2 The core of judicial ethics is fairness, integrity, and serving the people. The basic requirements are loyalty to the judicial cause, ensuring judicial fairness, ensuring judicial integrity, adhering to justice for the people, and maintaining the image of the judiciary.

Article 3 Judges shall conscientiously abide by judicial ethics, strictly demand of themselves in both their official duties and extra-professional activities, and uphold the image of the people's courts and judicial credibility.

Chapter II Loyalty to the Judicial Cause

Article 4 Firmly establish a socialist concept of the rule of law, be loyal to the Party, to the state, to the people, and to the law, and be a builder and defender of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Article 5 Uphold and maintain the socialist judicial system with Chinese characteristics, earnestly implement and enforce the basic strategy of governing the country according to law, respect and believe in the law, modelly abide by the law, strictly enforce the law, and conscientiously safeguard the authority and dignity of the law.

Article 6 Love the judicial cause, cherish the honor of being a judge, adhere to professional ethics, abide by judicial conscience, firmly establish the core values of the judiciary, take it as one's duty to uphold social fairness and justice, and earnestly fulfill the duties of a judge.

Article 7 Safeguard national interests, observe political discipline, protect state secrets and secrets concerning judicial work, refrain from engaging in or participating in activities that harm national interests and judicial authority, and refrain from making statements that harm national interests and judicial authority.

Chapter III Ensuring Judicial Fairness

Article 8 Uphold and maintain the principle that the people's courts independently exercise their adjudicative power according to law, hear cases objectively and fairly, engage in independent thinking and autonomous judgment during judicial activities, dare to adhere to principles, and not be interfered with by any administrative organ, social organization, or individual, or be influenced by factors such as power and personal relationships.

Article 9 Adhere to basing decisions on facts and taking law as the criterion, strive to ascertain case facts, accurately grasp the spirit of the law, correctly apply the law, reasonably exercise discretion, avoid subjective assumptions, exceeding authority, and abusing power, and ensure that case adjudications are fair and just.

Article 10 Firmly establish an awareness of procedural rules, emphasize both substantive justice and procedural justice, strictly follow statutory procedures in handling cases, fully protect the litigation rights of parties and other participants in proceedings, and avoid arbitrary conduct in case handling.

Article 11 Strictly observe statutory case handling time limits, improve the efficiency of trials and executions, resolve disputes promptly, pay attention to conserving judicial resources, and eliminate acts such as dereliction of duty and delaying case handling.

Article 12 Earnestly implement the principle of judicial openness, respect the people's right to know, consciously accept legal supervision and social supervision, and at the same time avoid improper external influence on judicial adjudication.

Article 13 Conscientiously abide by the system of judicial recusal, maintain a neutral and fair stance when hearing cases, treat parties and other participants in proceedings equally, without favoritism or discrimination against any party, and do not meet privately or alone with parties, their agents, or defenders.

Article 14 Respect the lawful exercise of adjudicative powers by other judges; except when performing work duties or through proper procedures, do not inquire into, interfere with, or comment on cases being tried by other judges.

Chapter IV Ensuring Judicial Integrity

Article 15 Foster a correct outlook on power, position, and interests; adhere to self-respect, self-examination, self-warning, and self-motivation; uphold the bottom line of integrity; correctly exercise adjudicative and enforcement powers according to law; and eliminate acts of abusing power for personal gain and taking bribes to pervert the law.

Article 16 Strictly abide by the provisions on integrity in the judiciary; do not accept invitations to meals or gifts from parties involved in a case or related persons; do not use one's position or status as a judge to seek improper benefits; do not engage in improper dealings with parties or other participants in proceedings in violation of regulations; and do not engage in malpractices for personal gain in case handling.

Article 17 Do not engage in or participate in for-profit business activities; do not concurrently hold positions such as legal counsel in enterprises or other for-profit organizations; and do not provide advisory opinions to parties or other participants in proceedings concerning pending cases or retrial cases.

Article 18 Properly handle personal and family affairs; do not use one's status as a judge to seek special benefits. Report personal matters as required by regulations, educate and urge family members not to use the judge's authority or status to seek improper benefits.

Chapter V Adhering to Justice for the People

Article 19 Firmly establish the concept of putting people first and justice for the people; strengthen the mass viewpoint; pay attention to the demands of the people; care about the feelings of the people; and conscientiously protect the legitimate rights and interests of the people.

Article 20 Give full play to the active role of the judiciary; actively seek dispute resolution methods conducive to case closure and dispute resolution; and strive to achieve the unity of legal effect and social effect.

Article 21 Earnestly implement the provisions on facilitating access to justice for the people; strive to provide necessary procedural convenience for parties and other participants in proceedings; and reduce their litigation costs as much as possible.

Article 22 Respect the dignity of the personality of parties and other participants in proceedings; avoid condescending attitudes and undesirable work styles such as "cold, hard, rude, and obstructive"; respect lawyers; and protect in accordance with law the rights of lawyers to participate in litigation activities.

Chapter VI Maintaining the Image of the Judiciary

Article 23 Persist in learning, diligently study professional matters, be devoted to one's duties, handle cases impartially, punish evil and promote good, uphold justice, and maintain a spirited mental state and good professional conduct.

Article 24 Adhere to civilized justice, observe judicial etiquette, behave properly, dress appropriately, use civilized language, and maintain a calm attitude in the course of performing duties, so as to maintain good professional cultivation and judicial style.

Article 25 Strengthen self-cultivation, cultivate noble moral character and healthy life interests, refrain from undesirable habits and conduct inconsistent with the professional image of a judge or contrary to judicial ethics, abide by social morality and family virtues, and maintain a good personal reputation.

Article 26 After retirement, judges shall comply with relevant state regulations, shall not use their former status or convenient conditions to inquire into or interfere with case handling, and shall avoid causing adverse effects on the professional image of judges due to improper personal words or deeds.

Chapter VII Supplementary Provisions

Article 27 People's assessors shall abide by this Code when performing adjudicative duties in accordance with law. Other staff of the people's courts shall implement this Code by reference.

Article 28 People's courts at all levels are responsible for supervising the implementation of this Code. Acts violating this Code shall be dealt with by means of admonitory talks, criticism, or circulars depending on the circumstances and consequences; where the circumstances are serious and constitute a disciplinary or legal violation, strict handling shall be carried out in accordance with relevant disciplinary regulations and legal provisions.

Article 29 This Code shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 30 This Code shall take effect as of the date of issuance. The Basic Code of Ethics for Judges of the People's Republic of China issued by the Supreme People's Court on October 18, 2001 shall be simultaneously abolished.
